title: Micro Experiment Snapshotbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal tracker for small inference experiments — compact table + scratch notes so I can iterate fast before formalizing in the bench harness. Kept intentionally messy.

Experiment goals:
- Find low-cost quantization setting that keeps p99 < 220ms for 512-token requests on A100-40G equivalent.
- Measure tokens/sec and estimate $/1000 tokens for different batch sizes.

Key: model shorthand: gpt-small-v1 (gs-v1), gs-v1-4q (4q), gs-v1-8q (8q)

Snapshot table (most recent runs on host: dev-a100-40g):
| run | date       | model   | quant | batch | seq | tokens/s | p50(ms) | p99(ms) | $/1k toks | note                       |
|-----|------------|---------|-------|-------|-----|----------|---------|--------:|----------:|----------------------------|
| r091| 2026-03-08 | gs-v1   | fp16  | 1     | 512 | 85       | 95      | 210     | 0.012     | baseline - no cache         |
| r092| 2026-03-09 | gs-v1   | 8q    | 1     | 512 | 120      | 75      | 180     | 0.007     | 8-bit quant, noticeable perf|
| r093| 2026-03-09 | gs-v1   | 4q    | 2     | 512 | 210      | 60      | 230     | 0.005     | batching improves throughput|
| r094| 2026-03-10 | gs-v1   | 8q    | 2     | 256 | 300      | 40      | 160     | 0.0035    | short seq helps, good p99   |
| r095| 2026-03-10 | gs-v1-x | 8q    | 2     | 512 | 190      | 70      | 195     | 0.0042    | kernel tweak applied        |

Quick observations (raw):
- 8q consistently increases tokens/s vs fp16; p99 drops in multiple configs.
- r093 p99 regression likely from sequence length + resource contention at batch=2; need to re-run with pinned cuda streams.
- Best cost/throughput in r094 for 256 seq but our target seq=512 for production.

Back-of-envelope cost calc: (simple)
- Assumptions: GPU cost baseline = $2.40/hr (equiv for test instance), tokens/s measured per GPU.
- $/1k toks = (GPU $/sec) / (tokens/sec) * 1000
Example r092: GPU $/sec = 2.40/3600 = 0.0006667; tokens/s =120 -> $/1k = 0.0006667/120*1000 = 0.00556 (~0.0056) -> matches measured 0.007 after adding infra overhead (~25%)

Quick TODOs (prioritized):
- [ ] Re-run r093 with CUDA stream pinning + cpu affinity (ticket local: bench/run-093)
- [ ] Add KV-prefix cache test (small prefix 64 tokens) for r094-like config
- [ ] Run same tests on 80GB instance to estimate linear scaling (r095-lite)
- [ ] Log exact kernel build flags used for r095 (kernel-optim-3)

Notes to self / weird bits:
- Observed occasional 3-4x jitter in p99 when other user jobs start on node; need to add node isolation flag next time.
- r092 CPU utilization low -> indicates memory-bound quant kernel; ask @Rhea to sanity-check memory copy pattern.
- Session artifacts: kept raw logs in /mnt/bench-logs/ethan/2026-03-09/ (compress later).

Slack/thread references:
- quick thread: #applied-ml: "8q-stability" (pt 9 Mar) -> pinned messages with traces
- note: DevOps asked to avoid dedicated execution on shared lab nodes after 18:00 UTC.

Questions to resolve before formalizing: Q1: Is p99 at batch=2 representative for our 99th while traffic spikes? (A: need synthetic spike test)
Q2: What % of quality drop from 8q vs fp16 (human eval)? Quick plan: sample 200 outputs for r092 and run micro-eval on rubric.

Micro-eval checklist (quick):
- create eval subset: 200 prompts (mix short/long) -> sample from prompt-bank/v1/seed-021
- collect outputs r092, r095 -> compute exact-match + fluency score (human)
- auto heuristics: embedding-similarity threshold 0.88 (cos sim) to flag regressions

Scratch ideas (future):
- small script to auto-calc $/1k across runs and plot delta vs p99 (cheap viz in colab)
- try hybrid config: prefix cache + 8q for long seqs, see if p99 stays < 220ms

File housekeeping:
- If this yields stable config (p99 < 220 @512 and $/1k < 0.005): promote to repo bench/configs/prod-512-8q.yaml and open PR to benchmarks.

End of snapshot.

CHANGES LOG (short):

- 2026-03-09: added quant runs r092,r093; flagged r093 p99 anomaly
- 2026-03-10: kernel tweak and short-seq experiments r094,r095; added TODOs and micro-eval plan

- local checklist: build-kernel -> run-smoke -> run-full -> collect-logs -> compress -> upload to s3://redwood-bench/ethan/
